# System Page Template (Business-User First)

Use this template for every system page in [`../systems/`](../systems/).

## Writing Intent

- Explain the system in plain business language first.
- Add technical details only when they improve decision-making.
- Always connect capability to measurable business value.

## Required Page Structure

Copy this section and replace placeholders.

```markdown
# <System Name>

## 1) What This System Is
Briefly define the system in one or two paragraphs.

## 2) Who Uses It
- Primary business users
- Secondary users (admins, operations, IT)

## 3) Business Problem It Solves
- Problem A
- Problem B
- Problem C

## 4) Core Capabilities
### Capability 1
What it does and why that matters for the business.

### Capability 2
What it does and why that matters for the business.

## 5) Major Benefits and Advantages
- Benefit 1 (outcome and impact)
- Benefit 2 (outcome and impact)
- Benefit 3 (outcome and impact)

## 6) Typical Business Scenarios
### Scenario: <Scenario Name>
- Trigger
- Workflow
- Expected outcome

## 7) Dependencies and Related Systems
- Upstream and downstream systems
- External services (if relevant)
- Critical operational dependencies

## 8) Success Indicators
- Adoption metrics
- Productivity metrics
- Quality/risk metrics

## Source Evidence
- Path: <repo/file/path>
- Path: <repo/file/path>

## Related Documentation
- Link 1
- Link 2
```

## Quality Checklist (Must Pass)

- The page can be understood by a non-technical business user.
- Every capability is linked to a business outcome.
- "Benefits and Advantages" section is explicit and substantive.
- Dependencies are clearly named and cross-linked.
- At least three practical scenarios or scenario variants are included.
- Source evidence paths are included and relevant.

## Style Rules

- Use concise headings and short paragraphs.
- Prefer active voice and direct wording.
- Avoid unexplained acronyms; define terms on first use.
- Use tables when comparing options or roles.
- Keep claims evidence-based and avoid marketing-only statements.
